extracted.intended_audience: readers, editors, and scholars of English literature and literary criticism; those evaluating editions, biographies, and critical notes
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for editing and critiquing literary works (editions, notes, biographies, translations) and for the ethical practice of satire and literary conduct. Emphasises factual accuracy, typographical care, stylistic clarity, fairness, and evidentiary rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: editorial_factual_accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The notes absolutely swarm with misstatements, into which the editor never would have fallen, if he had taken the slightest pains to investigate the truth of his assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and annotators must verify dates, facts, and identities before publication. The review gives multiple concrete anti-examples (wrong death dates for Derrick, Sir Herbert Croft, Sir William Forbes; inconsistent ages for Mrs. Thrale; mistaken claims about proprietorship of periodicals). Mistakes that a careful investigator would avoid are grounds for strong criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: typographical_execution
rubrics_metrics.description: In new editions of classical works it ought to be, almost faultless: the typographical execution would be, as in new editions of classical works it ought to be, almost faultless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality editions should have nearly flawless typography. Poor printing is an independent defect alongside errors of fact or arrangement; typographical care is expected for classical texts and scholarly editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: compilation_and_arrangement_quality
rubrics_metrics.description: This edition is ill compiled, ill arranged, ill written, and ill printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An editor's work should be well compiled (selecting and organizing material sensibly) and well arranged (logical order, useful apparatus). Bad compilation/arrangement undermines usability and scholarly value; reviewers will treat these as major faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: thorough_acquaintance_with_primary_texts
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor never would have fallen into such errors ... if he had even been well acquainted with the book on which he undertook to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before annotating or editing, the editor must read and understand the primary text(s) thoroughly. Ignorance of the work being edited leads to misreadings, misattributions, and misplaced notes—faults exemplified in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: clarity_and_precision_of_notes_and_style
rubrics_metrics.description: The style of the notes would be neat, clear, and precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotations and critical notes should be written with neatness, clarity, and precision. Style matters: neat, clear, and precise prose in footnotes/notes increases the value of an edition; slovenly or ambiguous notes harm the reader's understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: proper_attribution_and_contextual_interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If we apply the words 'little Dicky' to Steele, we deprive a very lively and ingenious passage, not only of all its wit, but of all its meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and editors must attribute phrases and nicknames correctly and interpret passages in their proper historical/contextual sense. Misattribution or decontextualised quoting can destroy an author's intended wit or meaning and spread false claims (the review documents repeated misreadings of 'little Dicky').

rubrics_metrics.name: evidentiary_standard_for_accusations_and_historical_claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any external evidence to support this grave accusation? The answer is short. There is absolutely none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious accusations (e.g., of conspiracy, fraud, or malice) require external, corroborating evidence. Absent such evidence, claims should not be asserted as fact. The reviewer treats unsupported insinuations as groundless and unfair.

rubrics_metrics.name: editorial_fairness_and_generosity
rubrics_metrics.description: No man in Addison's situation could have acted more fairly and kindly, both towards Pope and towards Tickell, than he appears to have done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors, patrons, and influential literary figures should act with fairness and generosity (e.g., lending aid, acknowledging merit) rather than pettiness. The reviewer praises Addison's fair conduct as a standard for behaviour in literary circles.

rubrics_metrics.name: ethical_use_of_satire
rubrics_metrics.description: The great satirist, who alone knew how to use ridicule without abusing it, who, without inflicting a wound, effected a great social reform, and who reconciled wit and virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire should aim at social correction rather than vindictive personal injury. Effective satirists use wit and ridicule in ways that maintain moral purpose and avoid gratuitous abuse; satire reconciles cleverness with ethical restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: maintain_good_taste_and_civility_in_argument
rubrics_metrics.description: He replied with severity, but, in our opinion, with less severity than was due ... nor did he, in his just anger, forget for a moment the laws of good taste and good breeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding to attacks or criticisms can be severe, but should remain within the bounds of good taste and civility. Rhetorical sharpness is acceptable when proportionate, but decorum and 'good breeding' are virtues in public literary disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: completeness_of_collected_works_and_editorial_scope
rubrics_metrics.description: We yet possess a complete collection of Addison's writings. This edition, though eminently beautiful, is in some important points defective; nor, indeed, do we yet possess a complete collection of Addison's writings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collected editions should strive for completeness and note known gaps. A beautiful presentation is insufficient if important writings are omitted or editorial defects persist; completeness and accurate representation of an author's corpus are criteria of scholarly editions.
